rows.question: How was the etcd database space exceeded problem fixed?
rows.answer:
Relevant evidence:
- #1003 etcd 'mvcc: database space exceeded' makes all API writes fail: compact to the current revision, run etcdctl defrag on each member, then etcdctl alarm disarm. Long term we raised --quota-backend-bytes to 8 GiB and enabled automatic compaction (--auto-compaction-retention=1h). [1]
- #1009 kube-apiserver requests fail with 'context deadline exceeded' when etcd is slow: etcd shared a disk with container logs. Moving the etcd data dir to a dedicated SSD brought fsync p99 under 10ms and the deadline errors disappeared. [2]
- #1017 Frequent etcd leader elections across availability zones: Tune --heartbeat-interval to about the RTT (e.g. 100ms) and --election-timeout to 10x that (1000ms). Check that disk fsync latency is also low. [3]

rows.question: Why do pods go into CrashLoopBackOff after a containerd upgrade and what is the fix?
rows.answer:
Relevant evidence:
- #1001 Pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after upgrading containerd to 1.7.20: set SystemdCgroup = true under the runc options in /etc/containerd/config.toml so containerd and the kubelet agree on the systemd cgroup driver, then restart containerd. Pods recover without being recreated. [1]
- #1012 ingress-nginx returns 502 Bad Gateway during rolling updates: add a preStop hook (sleep 10) and a readinessProbe so the pod is removed from endpoints before the app stops accepting connections. [2]
- #1006 kubelet reports 'PLEG is not healthy' on nodes with many containers: PLEG (pod lifecycle event generator) relists all containers from the runtime. Slow runtime or disk I/O makes the relist exceed the threshold. Reducing maxPods to 110 and moving /var/lib/containerd to local SSD fixed it for us. [3]

rows.question: How do I fix CoreDNS i/o timeout errors under load?
rows.answer:
Relevant evidence:
- #1004 CoreDNS i/o timeout resolving external names under load: scaled CoreDNS with the cluster-proportional-autoscaler, increased the cache plugin TTL to 30s and deployed NodeLocal DNSCache so most lookups never leave the node. Timeouts stopped. [1]
- #1022 Containers OOMKilled although working set is below the memory limit (cgroup v2): Size the JVM heap with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70 and leave headroom for page cache and off-heap memory; newer kernels reclaim page cache before OOM more reliably. [2]
- #1021 Slow DNS lookups because of ndots:5: set dnsConfig.options ndots: 2 on the pod spec, or use fully qualified names with a trailing dot. [3]

rows.question: Tell me about issue #1015
rows.answer:
Issue #1015 CoreDNS CrashLoopBackOff: Loop detected for zone: point the kubelet --resolv-conf at /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf (the real upstream servers) instead of the stub resolver, then restart CoreDNS.

Relevant evidence:
- #1015 CoreDNS CrashLoopBackOff: Loop detected for zone: point the kubelet --resolv-conf at /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf (the real upstream servers) instead of the stub resolver, then restart CoreDNS. [1]
- #1002 kube-scheduler leaves pods Pending with topologySpreadConstraints on tainted nodes: Workaround: set nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor in the topology spread constraint so tainted nodes the pod cannot tolerate are excluded from the skew calculation. [2]
- #1008 kube-proxy in IPVS mode drops connections after endpoint updates: Setting net.ipv4.vs.conntrack=1 and net.ipv4.vs.expire_nodest_conn=1 reduces resets; graceful termination of endpoints is the proper fix. [3]
